title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a faint draft. The next page appears to be a clean copy of the same computation, and it confirms most readings. The aim is to set up, in étale cohomology, the 'Picard / Albanese' part of the cycle and Lefschetz program. The previous page asks whether integral cycles realize the inverses of H^1(A_X)→H^1(X) and H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1)→H^1(B_X); this page computes the integral and torsion structure of those groups.

Setting: X proper over an algebraically closed field k, N prime to char k.

(1) Kummer sequence. Since H^0(X,G_m)=k^* is divisible, H^1(X,μ_N) ≅ Pic(X)[N].

(2) Exact sequence 0 → Pic^0(X)[N] → H^1(X,μ_N) → NS(X)[N] → 0. It is exact on the right because Pic^0(X)=Pic^0_{X/k}(k) is divisible.

(3) Tate modules. Taking the limit over ℓ^ν gives H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)) ≅ T_ℓ Pic(X) = T_ℓ(Pic^0_{X/k}). This uses the non-trivial fact that Pic^τ/Pic^0 is finite, so NS contributes nothing to the Tate module.

(4) Albanese comparison. If Pic^0_{X/k} is proper (e.g. X normal), put B_X = (Pic^0_{X/k})_red (an abelian variety) and A_X = B_X^* (the Albanese). Then the Albanese map φ_X: X → A_X induces an isomorphism φ_X^*: H^1(A_X,Z_ℓ) → H^1(X,Z_ℓ).

(5) Duality. For X smooth projective of dimension n, Poincaré duality gives H^{2n-1}(X,Z/N) ≅ H^1(X,Z/N)^∨(-n). Dualizing (2) gives 0 → (NS(X)[N])^∨ → H^{2n-1}(X,Z/N)(n-1) → (Pic^0[N])^∨ → 0. The Weil pairing identifies the last term with A_X[N] up to twist, or equivalently with H^1(B_X,Z/N).

(6) Limit over ℓ^ν. This gives 0 → (NS(X){ℓ})^∨ → H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1) → H^1(B_X,Z_ℓ) → 0. The left term is the finite ℓ-primary torsion and the right term is the free quotient. So the torsion of H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ) is the Pontryagin dual of the ℓ-torsion of NS, and the torsion-free quotient is H^1 of the Picard variety.

This is exactly the input needed to pose the previous page's question 2: can an integral cycle on B_X × X invert H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) → H^1(B_X)?
errors: The draft's twist bookkeeping is loose. H^1(X,Z_ℓ) ≅ T_ℓ Pic^0 should read H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)), as the clean copy writes. The sequence should be twisted so that H^{2n-1}(X)(n-1) maps onto H^1(B_X); the draft has ν A_X(k)(-n), which is consistent only after the Weil pairing twist.
The transcription of this page misreads Pic as Br and H^1 as H^2. Mathematically, the Brauer group plays no role here.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard computation of H^1 and H^{2n-1} via Kummer theory, the Picard scheme and Poincaré duality. It is a draft of the next page. The interesting integral-cycle questions sit on the neighbouring page, not here.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: '→ _nBr ... H^2(X,μ_n) → _n NS(X) → 0' should be '0 → _N Pic^0(X) → H^1(X,μ_N) → _N NS(X) → 0'.
Bracket: 'k séparablement clos' should be 'k alg. clos'.
'H^1(X,Z_ℓ) ≃ T_ℓ(Pic°)' is better read as H^1(X,Z_ℓ(1)) ≃ T_ℓ(Pic^0_{X/k}). The margin note concerns the finiteness of Pic^τ(X)/Pic^0(X).
'B_X = Pic°' should be 'B_X = Pic^{00}_{X/k}' (reduced), and 'A_X = B_X^*'. The arrow is labelled φ_X^*.
Final sequence: the left term is (NS(X){ℓ})^∨, marked 'comp. ℓ-primaire' (torsion), and the middle term is H^{2n-1}(X,Z_ℓ)(n-1).
